citations.title: Classes of operating certificates
citations.requirement: Lists the OPWDD operating certificate classes for community residences: supervised community residence, supportive community residence, and individualized residential alternative (IRA).

citations.title: Part 686 Glossary (IRA, supervised IRA, supportive IRA, protective oversight)
citations.requirement: Defines IRA and the supervised and supportive IRA types. A supervised IRA has staff onsite or proximately available whenever residents are present.

citations.title: Certification of the facility class known as individualized residential alternative
citations.requirement: (a)(2)-(3): 9+ persons must meet 635-7.1, 7.2 and 7.3. 8 or fewer persons must meet the 635-7.1(h)(1)(ii) building code (NYC: 635-7.1(i)(1)(ii)) and 635-7.4(b)(3). If occupants cannot evacuate in 3 minutes or less, 635-7.2(a)(1)(iii) also applies. (a)(4): an IRA must meet 686.1-686.5, 686.9, 686.15(a)(1)-(3) and 686.16. (a)(5)-(6): protective oversight appropriate to need, with a site-specific written plan covering assessment of each person's supervision need (staff and/or technology), trained substitutes, supervisor qualifications and training, and periodic review. (a)(7): MHL 41.34 site selection applies to 4-14 bed IRAs with onsite supervision and 1-3 bed IRAs with 24-hour supervision. (b): OPWDD verifies the facility evacuation plan, staff and resident training and evaluation, a current fire-evacuation evaluation in each ISP (8 or fewer beds), an annual review of each person's protective oversight plan, supervisor first-aid training, and fire alarms audible in sleeping areas with doors closed (8 or fewer beds).

citations.title: Utilization of temporary use beds and vacant beds
citations.requirement: IRAs of four or more beds may designate temporary use beds on the operating certificate. Temporary use beds count toward certified capacity. 686.15(a)(1)-(3) applies to IRAs through 686.16(a)(4).

citations.title: Staffing (community residences)
citations.requirement: (a)(1)-(2): personnel must be available to supervise, operate and maintain the premises, and there must be a staffing plan based on the number of individuals, their level of functioning and need, support staff needs and physical plant demands. (a)(3): volunteers may not substitute for paid personnel. Family and friends are not counted as volunteers. (a)(4): in a supervised residence, staff must be available whenever individuals are present. Less intensive coverage is allowed only on a documented individual assessment in the plan of services. (b)(1): a written staffing schedule at the site shows supervision available or on call 24 hours a day. (b)(2): a written volunteer utilization plan if volunteers are used. The rule sets no numeric ratio.

citations.title: Governance (community residences)
citations.requirement: Applies to IRAs via 686.16(a)(4). Section number and title are confirmed in the Part 686 table of contents. Section text was not fetched, so pull it before drafting governing-body content.

citations.title: Administration (community residences)
citations.requirement: Section number and title are confirmed in the Part 686 table of contents. Section text was not fetched. 686.6 is not listed in 686.16(a)(4), so confirm its applicability to IRAs before citing it as an IRA requirement.

citations.title: Fee-setting and financial reporting for voluntary-operated community residences
citations.requirement: Section number and title are confirmed in the Part 686 table of contents. Section text was not fetched. Applicability to IRAs is not confirmed because 686.13 is not listed in 686.16(a)(4).

citations.title: Recordkeeping (community residences)
citations.requirement: Section number and title are confirmed in the Part 686 table of contents. Section text was not fetched. It is not listed in 686.16(a)(4), so confirm applicability to IRAs.

citations.title: Physical plant, Life Safety Code and environmental requirements referenced by 686.16; Uniform Code enforcement for IRAs via 635-7.4(a)(3)
citations.requirement: Building, Life Safety Code and environmental standards that 686.16 incorporates for IRAs. NYS DOS guidance identifies 635-7.4(a)(3) as the Uniform Code enforcement route for OPWDD IRAs.

citations.title: Safety and welfare requirements for all facilities (except family care homes and IRAs housing eight or fewer persons)
citations.requirement: Applies to supervised community residences and IRAs housing nine or more persons. One listed requirement is documentation that all heat and smoke-detecting alarm devices are tested quarterly (635-7.3(e)(i)(1)).

citations.title: Rights and responsibilities of persons receiving services
citations.requirement: (a)(3): rights limitations must be documented, individual, time-limited and for clinical purposes only. (a)(4): enumerated rights (safe and sanitary environment; freedom from abuse, corporal punishment, unnecessary mechanical restraint and unnecessary medication; confidentiality; written individualized plan with right to participate, object and appeal; choice of physician and dentist; sexuality and family planning information; religion; voting; use of personal money; balanced diet; own clothing; privacy; storage; request an alternative residence; grievances without reprisal; visitors and communication; health care proxy; gender expression). (a)(4)(xv): information before admission on supplies and services provided and charges. (a)(6): staff are advised of rights. (a)(7): rights are not limited for staff convenience, as a threat, as retribution or for discipline. (a)(8): rights and conduct rules are given at or before admission and after changes, in the primary language. (a)(9): objections under 633.12. (a)(10): written requests for clinical record access under MHL 33.16, with denial review by the OPWDD Clinical Record Access Review Committee. (a)(11): health care proxy duties. (a)(12): advise of complaint contacts on admission and as they change. (a)(15): language access with no charge for interpreters.

citations.title: Training of employees, volunteers, family care providers and persons receiving services with regard to their safety and the prevention of abuse
citations.requirement: (b)(1): training within 3 months of hire or start of volunteering on human growth and development, characteristics of persons served, promoting positive relationships, abuse prevention/identification/reporting/processing, laws and policies on protection from abuse, incident reporting, and safety and security procedures including fire safety. (b)(2): annual retraining on positive relationships, abuse prevention and reporting, laws and policies, incident reporting, and safety/security including fire safety. (a)(1)(viii)-(ix): training on preventing and managing significant-risk body substance exposure (HIV). (b)(3): a mechanism to monitor type, frequency and amount of training, with current records and employee concurrence on interview. (a)(2), (b)(4): self-protection training for individuals identified by the program planning team. (b)(5): one-time board training applies only to not-for-profit corporations.

citations.title: Management of personal funds
citations.requirement: Applies to all OPWDD-certified residential facilities. Policies must reflect the agency's fiduciary duty under MHL 33.07(e) when it manages funds. Policies must address at minimum security, staff accountability, paper and electronic recordkeeping, usage, and monitoring of personal allowance and other income. Personal allowance is the monthly income portion for the individual's personal expenditure. Management is the SSL 131-o offer to set up separate accounting. Records of compliance are kept 4 years per OPWDD's regulations page. Only excerpts of the section were retrieved.

citations.title: Protection of individuals receiving services in facilities operated and/or certified by OPWDD (behavior support)
citations.requirement: Applies to all OPWDD-certified residential facilities. Definitions reviewed: behavior plan/human rights committee; informed consent committee; functional behavior assessment; behavior support plan as a component of the plan of services; restrictive/intrusive interventions (intermediate and restrictive physical intervention, exclusionary time-out, mechanical restraining devices, behavior medication without a co-occurring psychiatric diagnosis, and other agency-designated methods); physical intervention categories (protective, intermediate, restrictive); modified clothing as a mechanical restraint; rights limitations; aversive conditioning; Level 1 and Level 2 Behavioral Intervention Specialist qualifications; program planning team composition. Operative subdivisions (d)-(j) were not retrieved.

citations.title: Medication (including vitamins)
citations.requirement: Required of all residential facilities. Each agency develops its own medication policies. Staff may administer only if they hold a job description with direct care duties and have completed an OPWDD-approved course and practicum and been certified or recertified within the year (a)(14)(iii)(c). Medical or nursing supervision of medication staff is required (a)(15). A program planning team evaluates self-administration ability with RN, physician or PA input, no later than 3 months after admission, and reviews it at least annually (a)(16). A separate administration record per person (name, medication/dose/route, date/time, signature) is required (a)(17). Annual medication regimen review by an RN, physician, PA or pharmacist (a)(18). Locked storage; double-locked controlled substances (non-supportive residences); separate locked container for medications in a food refrigerator (a)(19). OTC medication needs written practitioner approval at least annually and is limited to 2 days without practitioner direction (a)(13). Medication is suspended and the practitioner told immediately on a significant adverse reaction (a)(14)(ii). Disposal rules in (a)(20) were only partly retrieved.

citations.title: Criminal history record checks
citations.requirement: Applies to OPWDD-certified facilities and HCBS waiver services. (c)(1): designate authorized parties and submit their name, position and contact information to the Justice Center. (c)(2): written policies covering which applicants are subject to checks, safety and oversight of temporarily approved provisional staff and volunteers, notification to the Justice Center when a party ceases to be a subject party, and handling of later convictions or pending charges. (d)(2): checks are required for prospective employees and operators (natural persons with an ownership interest) with regular and substantial unsupervised contact. This is presumed for direct care in residential facilities (ICFs, CRs, IRAs), residential habilitation staff, supervisors of direct care staff, drivers and escorts, clinicians, care managers, and anyone assigned to a certified site. Also required on a change in ownership. (e): process under Part 701 (701.5). (f): provisional approval is allowed only without unsupervised physical contact, with monitoring by a trained employee and an attestation. Only the first part of the section was retrieved.

citations.title: [Expired] Training Flexibilities
citations.requirement: The Cornell LII Part 633 table of contents lists this section as [Expired]. The earlier research described commissioner flexibilities during extreme staffing shortages. Do not build any policy on it. Staff must complete the full 633.8 and 633.17 training.

citations.title: Notable occurrences, defined
citations.requirement: On and after 1/1/2016: serious notable occurrences are (a) the death of any person receiving services regardless of cause, including all deaths of residents of OPWDD-certified residences, and (b) sensitive situations, which agency policy must define and which include possible criminal acts by an individual. Minor notable occurrences are suspected theft or financial exploitation over $15 and up to $100 (isolated, no card involved) and injury needing treatment beyond first aid by a physician, dentist, PA or NP. A death that is also a reportable incident is reported both ways. The pre-2016 text, retained in the section, covered unauthorized absence, choking and larger thefts, which are now reportable incidents under 624.3.

citations.title: Reporting, recording, and investigation
citations.requirement: (a)(1): written policies on reporting, recording, investigation, review and monitoring; the reporting duties of employees, interns, volunteers, consultants and contractors; and notice to employees that every reportable incident is investigated and that an investigation continues to a substantiated or unsubstantiated finding even if the employee leaves. All employees, interns, volunteers, consultants and contractors must report. Minor notable occurrences go to the CEO or designee within 48 hours. Reportable incidents and serious notable occurrences go to the CEO or designee immediately, and to OPWDD immediately. IRMA updates are due at least monthly until closure. Only the first part of the section was retrieved from search text.

citations.title: Reportable incidents, defined
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced in 624.4 and 624.5. The section text was not fetched, so the current categories (abuse/neglect and significant incidents such as missing person, choking with known risk and inappropriate use of restraints) must be pulled from the regulation before drafting definitions.

citations.title: The Part 624 and Part 625 Handbook
citations.requirement: OPWDD guidance. Reportable incidents in OPWDD-certified programs go to the Justice Center VPCR at 1-855-373-2122 and to OPWDD under 624.5. Deliberate inappropriate use of restraints is abuse/neglect. Inappropriate use of restraints is a significant incident.

citations.cite: NYS Justice Center - Mandated Reporters (VPCR hotline)
citations.title: Mandated Reporters
citations.requirement: Employees and volunteers of certified or operated facilities are mandated reporters. They report when they have reasonable cause to suspect a reportable incident, via the 24-hour VPCR hotline at 1-855-373-2122 (Relay: dial 711 and give the number).

citations.cite: NYS Justice Center Criminal Background Check (CBC) program; MHL 16.33
citations.title: Criminal Background Check (CBC)
citations.requirement: Providers designate Authorized Persons to register applicants for fingerprinting (IdentoGO) and receive results.

citations.title: Criminal history checks for prospective OPWDD employees and volunteers
citations.requirement: OPWDD providers request checks for prospective employees and volunteers, submitted through OPWDD per the Justice Center CBC page. The statute text was not fetched; the cite and its application are taken from the research and the Justice Center page.

citations.title: Person-centered planning; Documentation of rights modifications
citations.requirement: From OPWDD's final regulation text, effective 11/1/2015. Applies to OPWDD-funded HCBS waiver services. The plan must document, for a certified residential setting, that the residence was chosen by the individual and which alternatives were considered. The plan is updated when it is ineffective and on reassessment of functional need. 636-1.4: modifications to the specified HCBS rights need a specific assessed need and justification in the person-centered service plan. 633.4 and 633.16 hold the related documentation rules.

citations.title: HCBS general requirements (integrated settings)
citations.requirement: From an OPWDD regulatory filing excerpt. HCBS must be delivered in integrated settings that do not isolate individuals. Setting qualities include a physically accessible setting. Any modification must be supported by a specific assessed need, justified and documented. Confirm against the current codified text, as this was a filing excerpt.

citations.title: Admission to and services in certified residential opportunities
citations.requirement: Subpart 636-3 (effective 3/14/2023) governs admission. OPWDD assigns Emergency Need, Substantial Need or Current Need. Certified residences must promptly report vacancies so each is first considered for people with Emergency Need.

citations.title: Responsibilities of care management providers
citations.requirement: Care managers confirm OPWDD eligibility and a residential request before referral.

citations.title: Residential habilitation in a community residence under the OPWDD HCBS waiver
citations.requirement: Defines residential habilitation in a community residence under the OPWDD 1915(c) HCBS waiver. Providers must be approved by OPWDD and DOH and be Medicaid-enrolled to be paid.

citations.title: Rates for residential habilitation services
citations.requirement: One provider-wide residential habilitation rate per provider.

citations.title: Supervised IRA residential habilitation: daily unit, rate codes, retainer days
citations.requirement: Daily unit of service. Rate codes cover service day, therapeutic/non-medical leave day and retainer/medical leave day. At most 14 retainer days per person per rate year. Research flags that it is not confirmed still in effect.

citations.title: IRA Residential Habilitation Service Documentation
citations.requirement: Dated guidance on IRA residential habilitation documentation. Research flags the supportive IRA 11-day minimum as status-unverified. Confirm it is current before use.

citations.cite: OMIG Audit Protocol - OPWDD IRA Residential Habilitation
citations.title: OMIG audit protocol
citations.requirement: OMIG audits IRA residential habilitation claims for documentation and rate-code compliance. A claim is disallowed if the documentation does not match the rate code billed.

citations.title: Personal allowance and room and board cost responsibilities
citations.requirement: Sets resident room and board and cost-of-care responsibilities and the personal allowance. For community residences including IRAs, the maximum monthly cost of care is the Level II SSI combined payment level minus the SSL 131-o minimum personal allowance. Supervised IRAs are responsible for required supplies and services under 635.9.

citations.cite: OPWDD Personal Allowance Manual (2023) and Protecting Personal Allowance advisory (Oct 2023)
citations.title: Personal allowance guidance
citations.requirement: Providers must have written procedures to handle, store and audit personal allowance. Staff are trained on them. Each person's funds are tracked separately. Funds are locked with limited access and staff accountability. There is a ledger of all receipts, disbursements and cash balance. Cash equivalents such as prepaid cards are treated as cash. Cash above the cash cap needs documentation of a specific purpose and is limited to 14 days. Annual personal expenditure planning is required when the agency manages the allowance.

citations.title: Fire safety: evacuation and fire drill frequency
citations.requirement: Standardizes minimum frequencies of evacuation and fire drills in homes and day settings. Evacuation and fire drills are generally procedurally synonymous. Drills may be varied for a few specific reasons, but the minimum number of full evacuation drills must still be met. Homes certified under the Health Care chapters of the Life Safety Code cannot use defend-in-place for non-fire evacuations. The numeric minimums were not captured, so pull the ADM text.

citations.cite: OPWDD Health and Safety Alert (July 2018) - HCBS Settings 'access to food'; 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi); 14 NYCRR 636-1.4
citations.title: Access to food in HCBS settings
citations.requirement: Individuals are entitled to access to food at any time. Restrictions run from least restrictive (all foods, all the time) to most restrictive through the person-centered planning process, and must be justified under 636-1.4.

citations.title: IRA Operating Certificate Application
citations.requirement: IRA operating certificate application. Listed processing time is 90 to 120 days. The term is triennial, with a maximum of 3 years. Denials are based on the inspection outcome.

citations.cite: eMedNY OPWDD Waiver Provider Enrollment; Community Residence enrollment (category of service 0269)
citations.title: Provider enrollment
citations.requirement: Enrollment requires an IRS SS-4 letter (a W-9 is not accepted) and certification of a Provider Compliance Program. Community residence enrollment is filed under category of service 0269.

citations.title: IRA Facilities
citations.requirement: A 1994 NYC DOB notice tied the final Certificate of Occupancy for IRAs to the IRA license. Current status is unverified, so ask DOB.

citations.title: Site selection (as applied to IRAs by 14 NYCRR 686.16(a)(7))
citations.requirement: Applies to IRAs of 4-14 beds with onsite supervision and 1-3 beds with 24-hour supervision, per 686.16(a)(7). The statute text was not fetched.

citations.cite: OPWDD memo to provider associations (Sept 2026) - new 14 NYCRR 633.9 / conforming changes to 633.15
citations.title: Representative payee rulemaking
citations.requirement: OPWDD is amending Part 633 to add or amend 633.9 on representative payees for residents of certified residences, with conforming changes to 633.15 on managing personal allowance. Confirm the adopted text before finalizing the funds policy.

citations.title: Mandated reporter definition and duty to report to the Justice Center
citations.requirement: Secondary source (Albany Law Government Law Center explainer endnotes) points to SSL 491 for mandated reporting and SSL 488(5), (5-a) for the definition. Statute text was not fetched.

citations.cite: Jonathan's Law (per NYS Justice Center Investigations Guidance, 2025)
citations.title: Notification and access to incident information
citations.requirement: Jonathan's Law requires notification and access to information about incidents at OPWDD-certified, operated or licensed providers. The statute section number is not stated in the retrieved text. Pull the statute and 624.5 for notice timeframes.

citations.cite: OPWDD Request for Approval to Fill a Residential Opportunity
citations.title: DDRO Director approval of placements
citations.requirement: Every placement into a certified residence requires approval of the DDRO Director before admission, using OPWDD's request form.

citations.cite: NYS Justice Center - What to Expect if You Are Involved in a Justice Center Investigation (Oct 2021)
citations.title: Mandated reporter timing; Category 2 findings
citations.requirement: A mandated reporter with reasonable cause to suspect a reportable incident reports immediately to the VPCR. Reporting may be delayed for safety or to call 911, but the report must be made within 24 hours of discovery. A final Category 2 finding is reported to OPWDD providers in the Staff Exclusion List check. It is not an automatic bar to employment but is a factor in the hiring decision.

policies.title: Organization, Governance and Residence Administration (Program Director)
state_specifics: An IRA must meet 14 NYCRR 686.1-686.5, 686.9, 686.15(a)(1)-(3) and 686.16 (686.16(a)(4)). Draft the governance content from the text of 686.5, which was not fetched.
686.6 Administration is not in the 686.16(a)(4) list. Confirm applicability before citing it.

'Operator' for background checks means any natural person with an ownership interest. Owners with regular and substantial contact need a 633.22 check, and so does any new owner after a change in ownership.
The board training in 633.8(b)(5) applies only to not-for-profit corporations. It does not apply to an LLC.
Designate the Authorized Party for criminal history checks and register the name, position and contact information with the Justice Center (633.22(c)(1)).
VERIFY: no OPWDD program director or manager qualification standard was found in the reviewed rules. Obtain OPWDD's written position.

policies.title: Operating Certificate, Waiver Enrollment and Provider Agreements
state_specifics: Class: IRA (supervised or supportive), certified by OPWDD under 14 NYCRR 619.2 and 686.16. Use the OMR 248 application. Listed processing is 90 to 120 days. The certificate is triennial, with a maximum term of 3 years. Denials are based on the inspection outcome.
Post the operating certificate and calendar renewal 6 to 12 months before expiry.

Size tiers: 8 or fewer persons use the 635-7.1(h)(1)(ii) building code (NYC: 635-7.1(i)(1)(ii)) plus 635-7.4(b)(3). 9+ persons must meet 635-7.1, 7.2 and 7.3. If residents cannot evacuate in 3 minutes or less, 635-7.2(a)(1)(iii) also applies.
MHL 41.34 site selection applies to 4-14 bed IRAs with onsite supervision and 1-3 bed IRAs with 24-hour supervision (686.16(a)(7)).

Waiver residential habilitation requires OPWDD and DOH approval plus Medicaid enrollment. Community residence enrollment is filed under category of service 0269. Waiver enrollment requires an IRS SS-4 letter and Provider Compliance Program certification.

OPWDD main office: 44 Holland Avenue, Albany NY 12229-0001, (866) 946-9733. The DQI area offices handle survey and deficiency disputes. The North Area (Schenectady) number is (518) 388-1441. OPWDD publishes a deficiency dispute process effective 4/1/2024.
NYC sites: confirm with DOB whether the 1994 notice (TPPN 9/94) still ties the Certificate of Occupancy to the IRA license.

policies.title: Policy Review, Document Control and Regulation-Mandated Policy Inventory
state_specifics: Regulations require the agency to have its own written policies for: reporting and investigating incidents (624.5(a)); medication (633.17(a)(5)); criminal history checks and provisional staff (633.22(c)(2)); personal funds (633.15(a)(3)); rights notification (633.4(a)(8)); and the definition of sensitive situations (624.4).
Keep a policy-to-citation matrix and a log of regulatory changes. Watch the pending Part 633 changes to 633.9 and 633.15 (OPWDD memo, Sept 2026).
Staff must be kept apprised of current policies on protection from abuse (633.8(a)(4)).

policies.title: Quality Improvement, Data Review and Mortality Review
state_specifics: Review incident data entered in IRMA. Updates are due at least monthly until each incident or serious notable occurrence is closed (624.5).
Every death of a person living in a certified residence is a serious notable occurrence and must be reviewed. Review it with the incident record.
Protective oversight plans must be reviewed at least annually and revised as needed (686.16(b)(3)).
VERIFY: no OPWDD mortality-review rule was retrieved. Confirm OPWDD's current mortality review expectations for voluntary providers before finalizing.
Track corrective action plans to closure, and train staff on trends (633.8(b)(2)).
